hero.title: AI medical scribe built for real clinical work
hero.subtitle: DocNote listens during the consultation, drafts the note, and lets you get back to the patient.
hero.lead: Physicians in Switzerland and across Europe use DocNote to turn spoken encounters into structured clinical documents (consultation notes, discharge letters, ward-round notes, operative reports) in seconds, not evenings.

story.title: One assistant, every document your practice actually ships
paragraphs: Most ambient scribes are built around a single US outpatient SOAP template. DocNote is different: it was designed in Switzerland by a doctor who wanted to stop losing evenings to paperwork, so it covers the documents European clinicians and hospitals produce every day.

Start a recording on mobile or web during the consultation. When the visit ends, DocNote turns the conversation into a structured draft that matches the note type you selected: consultation note, discharge letter, ward-round note, or operative report.

You then read the draft, correct anything that needs correcting, and validate it. Only the version you approve becomes part of the medical record, the same responsibility you already carry, just with far less typing.

sections.heading: Trimming long histories without losing detail
sections.body: First neurological consultations often produce very long drafts because the history of present illness carries many details. DocNote structures that detail so the neurologist can trim purposefully, without accidentally losing relevant findings.

sections.heading: Consults across departments
sections.body: A neurology consult on a different ward often follows a different structure than an outpatient consultation. DocNote adapts the template to the context while the underlying documentation logic stays consistent across both settings.

sections.heading: Structuring a detailed neurological exam
sections.body: A full neurological exam covers cranial nerves, motor, sensory, reflexes, coordination, and gait: a lot of discrete findings that are easy to lose in free text. DocNote keeps each category distinct in the draft, so a normal finding and an abnormal one are equally easy to find on review.

sections.heading: Chronic condition follow-up over time
sections.body: Conditions like migraine, epilepsy, or multiple sclerosis are tracked across many visits rather than resolved in one. Consistent structure across those visits makes it easier to see what has actually changed since the last consultation, instead of re-reading an entire history each time.

sections.heading: Connecting neurology consults to imaging and EMG
sections.body: Neurological assessment often depends on imaging or EMG results that live in separate systems. DocNote's note captures what was discussed about those findings during the encounter, while the source reports themselves stay in their own systems; the two are meant to complement each other, not merge into one tool.

sections.heading: Supporting complex differential diagnosis
sections.body: Neurology frequently involves a broad differential that narrows over several visits and tests. A structured Assessment section that the neurologist can revise consultation by consultation makes that evolving reasoning easier to follow later than a fresh, disconnected note each time.

sections.heading: Documenting for multidisciplinary care
sections.body: Many neurological conditions are managed alongside physiotherapy, psychiatry, or rehabilitation teams who need to read the neurologist's assessment quickly. Clear, structured notes make it easier for that wider team to stay aligned on the current plan without needing a separate summary meeting for every update or minor adjustment.

sections.heading: Fitting into an existing neurology workflow
sections.body: Most neurology services introduce DocNote alongside their current documentation habits rather than replacing them overnight, starting with outpatient follow-up visits before extending to first consultations and inpatient work.
